name: Live Quiz Battle
about: General knowledge, science, technology, mathematics, history, geography and logical reasoning. Facts chosen because they do not change. Each fact has a reference page (sourceUrl); arithmetic and reasoning questions are marked computed, with the working in the explanation. The answer is given as the text of the right option.

questions.prompt: Which part of a cell is known as its powerhouse?
questions.explanation: Mitochondria make most of the cell's supply of ATP, its energy currency.

questions.prompt: What is the chemical symbol for gold?
questions.explanation: Au comes from aurum, Latin for gold.

questions.prompt: What is the SI unit of force?
questions.explanation: One newton accelerates one kilogram at one metre per second squared.

questions.prompt: Which gas do plants take in for photosynthesis?
questions.explanation: Plants turn carbon dioxide and water into sugars, giving off oxygen.

questions.prompt: Which planet is known as the Red Planet?
questions.explanation: Iron oxide on its surface gives Mars its reddish colour.

questions.prompt: Which is the largest planet in our solar system?
questions.explanation: Jupiter's mass is more than twice that of all the other planets combined.

questions.prompt: About how fast does light travel in a vacuum?
questions.explanation: Exactly 299,792,458 metres per second.

questions.prompt: Which is the hardest naturally occurring substance?
questions.explanation: Diamond is 10, the top of the Mohs hardness scale.

questions.prompt: How many bones are there in a typical adult human body?
questions.explanation: A newborn has around 270; many fuse to give 206 in an adult.

questions.prompt: What is the pH of pure water at 25 °C?
questions.explanation: Pure water is neutral: pH 7 at 25 °C.

questions.prompt: What is the SI unit of electrical resistance?
questions.explanation: Resistance is measured in ohms (Ω).

questions.prompt: Which is the largest animal alive today?
questions.explanation: Blue whales reach about 30 m in length; the whale shark is the largest fish.

questions.prompt: What does CPU stand for?
questions.explanation: The CPU carries out a program's instructions.

questions.prompt: How many bits make one byte?
questions.explanation: The byte is standardised as eight bits.

questions.prompt: What does HTML stand for?
questions.explanation: HTML is the markup language of web pages.

questions.prompt: Which HTTP status code means "Not Found"?
questions.explanation: 404: the server cannot find the requested resource.

questions.prompt: What is the default port for HTTPS?
questions.explanation: HTTP uses 80 by default; HTTPS uses 443.

questions.prompt: How many bits long is an IPv4 address?
questions.explanation: IPv4 addresses are 32 bits; IPv6 addresses are 128 bits.

questions.prompt: Which data structure works on Last In, First Out?
questions.explanation: The last item pushed onto a stack is the first popped off.

questions.prompt: What is the time complexity of binary search on a sorted array?
questions.explanation: Each step halves the part of the array still to search.

questions.prompt: Which of these sorting algorithms is O(n log n) even in its worst case?
questions.explanation: Quicksort's worst case is O(n²); bubble and insertion sort are O(n²).

questions.prompt: Who created the Python programming language?
questions.explanation: Guido van Rossum released Python in 1991.

questions.prompt: Who wrote "Jana Gana Mana", India's national anthem?
questions.explanation: Written by Rabindranath Tagore; adopted as the national anthem in 1950.

questions.prompt: "Wings of Fire" is the autobiography of which Indian scientist and former President?
questions.explanation: Wings of Fire (1999), written with Arun Tiwari.

questions.prompt: What is the currency of Japan?
questions.explanation: The won is South Korea's; the yuan (renminbi) is China's.

questions.prompt: How many players does a cricket team have on the field?
questions.explanation: Each side fields eleven players.

questions.prompt: What is the national animal of India?
questions.explanation: The Bengal tiger; the peacock is the national bird.

questions.prompt: In which year did India become independent?
questions.explanation: 15 August 1947. The Constitution came into force on 26 January 1950.

questions.prompt: Who chaired the Drafting Committee of the Constitution of India?
questions.explanation: Rajendra Prasad presided over the Constituent Assembly; Ambedkar chaired its Drafting Committee.

questions.prompt: The Dandi March of 1930 was a protest against a tax on what?
questions.explanation: Gandhi's Salt March defied the British salt tax.

questions.prompt: Which Mughal emperor built the Taj Mahal?
questions.explanation: Built in memory of his wife Mumtaz Mahal.

questions.prompt: In which year did humans first land on the Moon?
questions.explanation: Apollo 11 landed on 20 July 1969.

questions.prompt: What is the capital of Australia?
questions.explanation: Canberra, not Sydney, is the capital.

questions.prompt: Which is the largest ocean on Earth?
questions.explanation: The Pacific covers about a third of Earth's surface.

questions.prompt: Which is the highest mountain above sea level?
questions.explanation: Everest is 8,849 m above sea level.

questions.prompt: Which is the largest hot desert in the world?
questions.explanation: Antarctica is the largest desert overall; the Sahara is the largest hot one.

questions.prompt: In the model taught in Indian schools, how many continents are there?
questions.explanation: Asia, Africa, North America, South America, Antarctica, Europe and Australia.

questions.prompt: In which city is the Taj Mahal?
questions.explanation: On the bank of the Yamuna in Agra, Uttar Pradesh.

questions.prompt: What is 20% of 250 plus 15% of 200?
What is the simple interest on ₹5,000 at 8% a year for 3 years?
What is the LCM of 12 and 18?
questions.explanation: 12 = 2²·3 and 18 = 2·3², so the LCM is 2²·3² = 36.

questions.prompt: What is the HCF of 48 and 180?
questions.explanation: 48 = 2⁴·3 and 180 = 2²·3²·5, so the HCF is 2²·3 = 12.

questions.prompt: A train 150 m long passes a pole in 15 seconds. What is its speed?
6 workers finish a job in 12 days. How many days would 9 workers take at the same rate?
A price rises by 10% and then falls by 10%. What is the overall change?
Two fair dice are rolled. What is the probability that the total is 7?
questions.explanation: 6 of the 36 equally likely outcomes total 7.

questions.prompt: What is the smaller angle between the hands of a clock at 3:30?
questions.explanation: The hour hand is at 105°, the minute hand at 180°: 75° apart.

questions.prompt: 10 people each shake hands once with every other person. How many handshakes are there?
What comes next: 2, 6, 12, 20, 30, ?
questions.explanation: The gaps are 4, 6, 8, 10, so the next gap is 12.

questions.prompt: If CAT is written as DBU, how is DOG written?
questions.explanation: Each letter moves one place forward.

questions.prompt: Today is Monday. What day will it be 61 days from today?
questions.explanation: 61 days is 8 weeks and 5 days; Monday + 5 days = Saturday.

questions.prompt: You face north, turn right, turn right again, then turn left. Which way do you face?
questions.explanation: North → East → South → East.

questions.prompt: A is taller than B, B is taller than C, and D is taller than A. Who is the shortest?
questions.explanation: D > A > B > C.

questions.prompt: What comes next: A, C, F, J, O, ?
questions.explanation: The gaps grow by one: +2, +3, +4, +5, +6.
